newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stocks close down, hit by profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stocks close down, hit by profit-taking.

text.p: Brazilian stocks closed sharply lower Wednesday, stung by a bout of profit-taking that was fueled by sharp losses on Wall Street, traders said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most-active stocks fell 2.59 percent to 9317 on heavy volume of 936 million reais ($891 million).
Traders said the market tried to rally back at midday, but the mood turned sour on a weak Dow, which was down 60 points at the Bovespa close.
"We were all expecting a round of profit-taking at one point and it finally happened," said one trader.
Bluechips were down across the board, without any particular news affecting individual stocks, traders said.
Benchmark Telebras preferred shares closed off 2.78 percent at 111.90, with common shares losing 2.96 percent to 108.00.
CVRD preferred shares fell 1.51 percent to close at 26.10 and common shares were off 0.95 percent at 31.30.
Petrobras preferred shares lost 3.2 percent at 212, with common shares down 1.67 percent at 176.98.

The bolsa's Electrical Energy Index (IEE) fell 1.44 percent percent to close at 2609. The index, which includes the nine most liquid power stocks, was pulled down by losses in state-owned power company Eletrobras. Eletrobras preferred shares fell 3.35 percent to close at 490.
Traders said stocks would open Thursday with an eye to Wall Street as little local news was expected to guide the market.
